title: Book Three · Chapter 93: Eight More
story:
On Monday, Ronan and Leo return to the one-yuan book pile.

The seller remembers them. He points to a few new arrivals beside the old stories.

“More ordinary books,” he says.

Leo is already looking at the covers. He chooses one story, then another in the same series.

Ronan opens the first book. The first page is clear. He looks at a few pages near the middle and closes it.

Leo has chosen the next one. Soon eight books are beside the seller's chair: six stories and two books with travel pictures.

The two stories from the same series lie together. One has a small man on the cover, standing very close to a much larger dog.

“Does the dog come back in the other one?” Ronan asks.

“I don't know yet.”

Leo opens the second story near the front. He shows Ronan the same little man, now beside a tall gate.

“We can read them before Saturday.”

“If we have time.”

Ronan looks toward the travel books. The bright pictures are easier to show from the edge of a table.

He moves one story back under the other. The pile looks good together. He thinks about people opening several books, instead of choosing only one.

The seller puts a hand beside the pile.

“These eight?”

Ronan looks at Leo. Leo nods.

He still has the picture of a busy table in his head when he reaches for their money. He wants to carry the books home and make room for them beside the thirteen already waiting.

The boys count them together. Eight books cost eight yuan.

They pay from the shared thirty-four. Twenty-six yuan remain.

On the way home, Leo carries one of their cloth bags. Ronan carries the other.

“The travel books went,” Leo says. “People want pictures.”

“And stories. The first woman wanted animals.”

“We can look for more of those.”

Ronan thinks about the first four yuan in his hand. He wants another morning like that, with more people at the table.

At home, they add the eight books to the thirteen left from Saturday. Twenty-one books now.

They mark the new eight with B. That group has eighteen books in it. Ronan's old games book and Leo's railway and garden books make the other three.

The two bags cost no more today. The next table morning is already paid for too.

Ronan writes twenty-one beside stock and twenty-six beside shared cash. Neither boy takes any money for himself.

Leo looks at the Saturday page.

“I open at nine. You go at half past eight.”

Ronan nods. “Anna and I meet at the library.”

“I can do the first part here.”

They put the two names beside the two jobs again. Ronan leaves his bus money in his personal envelope.

In the afternoon, the man who bought the travel books passes the gate. He asks about the next sale.

“Saturday, nine to eleven,” Ronan says. “Leo will be here in the morning.”

The man looks at the larger pile inside the room.

“More pictures?”

“Some. We are still looking.”

“My relatives may want a few. I will ask them.”

He goes on. Ronan watches him turn the corner.

Leo lifts one eyebrow. “A few.”

“He liked the first two.”

“Then we need to be ready.”

Ronan turns back to the stock. He puts a travel picture book at the front, beside the price card.

Across the table, his notebook is open to Anna's morning. The day and time are still clear. He closes the cover, puts the new books inside the bags, and begins to count the pages in the first story.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

series＝系列；new arrival＝新到的东西；relative＝亲戚；stock＝库存。

## 理解问题

1. 追加八本书后，共同现金和库存各是多少？有没有再付袋子和下一次桌位费？
2. Ronan此时给顾客说了什么营业安排？他对Anna的约定是否已经改口？

## 读句子

**Neither boy takes any money for himself.**

拆开看：Neither boy / takes any money / for himself.

两个男孩都没有／拿走共同的钱／拿去自己花。
